source_batch.unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 2: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Apply the paying bank duty under Section 31 to funds, mandate and wrongful dishonour

facts.statement: Section 31 requires the drawee to pay when duly required if sufficient drawer funds are held and properly applicable to the cheque; on default it compensates the drawer for resulting loss or damage. Courseware distinguishes gross balances from funds properly available for that payment.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 155–156; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Section 31 requires the drawee to pay when duly required if sufficient drawer funds are held and properly applicable to the cheque; on default it compensates the drawer for resulting loss or damage. Courseware distinguishes gross balances from funds properly available for that payment.

payload.title: A balance enquiry is only part of the payment decision
payload.core_explanation_md:
A cheque-payment decision needs both **funds** and **authority**. Under Section 31, the drawee must have enough of the drawer's money properly available for the cheque and must be duly required to pay it. An apparent credit balance does not answer whether a court restraint, earmarking or other lawful restriction prevents its use.

The operational sequence is to inspect the payment instruction, establish the funds available for that instruction, and resolve any restriction before deciding. Checking only the balance can produce both a wrongful refusal and a payment the bank had no authority to make.

self_check.prompt_text: Why can sufficient gross balance still fail the Section 31 funds test?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The funds must also be properly applicable to that cheque; a lawful restriction can prevent their use.

payload.title: Wrongful dishonour concerns the drawer's resulting loss
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 31 links the drawee's default to compensation of the **drawer** for loss or damage caused by it. The relevant investigation records the cheque, the usable funds, the mandate, the reason for refusal and the loss attributed to that refusal.

Do not treat the cheque amount as an automatic fixed compensation award. Nor should the file assume that the named payee is the statutory claimant under this particular section. Other causes of action need their own legal analysis; the immediate task is to apply Section 31 to the correct relationship and consequences.

self_check.prompt_text: Is compensation under Section 31 automatically equal to the cheque amount?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The section addresses the drawer's loss or damage caused by the default.

payload.stem_md: A customer has a credit balance sufficient for a cheque, but the bank has a binding court restraint covering those funds. Which fact is missing from a trainee's instruction to pay solely because the balance is adequate?

options.text_md: Whether the funds are properly applicable to this payment
options.explanation_md: Section 31 requires usable funds for the cheque, not merely a sufficient gross account balance.

options.text_md: Whether the gross credit balance exceeds the cheque amount by a large margin
options.explanation_md: A larger gross balance does not make funds properly applicable while the binding restraint remains.

options.text_md: Whether the cheque has travelled by paper rather than image
options.explanation_md: The transmission route does not remove the lawful restraint on the funds.

options.text_md: Whether the customer will indemnify the bank for ignoring the restraint
options.explanation_md: A customer indemnity does not itself permit the bank to disregard a binding court restraint.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 31 requires usable funds for the cheque, not merely a sufficient gross account balance.

payload.stem_md: A bank wrongfully refuses a duly payable cheque and the drawer proves loss caused by the refusal. Which statement describes Section 31's compensation relationship?

options.text_md: The payee automatically receives twice the cheque amount
options.explanation_md: Section 31 does not create this automatic payee award; it addresses the drawer's resulting loss.

options.text_md: The clearing house must compensate every former holder
options.explanation_md: The section places the relevant duty on the drawee toward the drawer, not on the clearing house toward all holders.

options.text_md: The drawee must compensate the drawer for the resulting loss or damage
options.explanation_md: That is the relationship and causal loss specified by Section 31.

options.text_md: No compensation is possible once the bank later apologises
options.explanation_md: A later apology does not eliminate loss or damage caused by the bank's default.

payload.correct_explanation_md: That is the relationship and causal loss specified by Section 31.

payload.stem_md: An internal review finds sufficient usable drawer funds, a duly issued payment instruction and no lawful reason for refusal. Which proposed conclusion needs correction?

options.text_md: The refusal should be investigated against the duty to pay
options.explanation_md: Those facts engage Section 31; investigation of the refusal against that duty is appropriate.

options.text_md: A cheque may always be refused at the bank's unrestricted discretion
options.explanation_md: Section 31 imposes a duty when its conditions are satisfied; it is not an unrestricted choice.

options.text_md: The file should preserve evidence of any loss caused to the drawer
options.explanation_md: Resulting loss or damage matters to the compensation required on default.

options.text_md: The bank should record the actual reason the cheque was refused
options.explanation_md: Recording the reason helps determine whether the refusal was justified and supports the causal investigation.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 31 imposes a duty when its conditions are satisfied; it is not an unrestricted choice.
